Company's own PBoC central-parity rate on 24 Aug 2026 for the interim dividend was 1.1555 (RMB0.14 -> HK$0.1618), consistent with CNY appreciation since. inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency: 10y China Government Bond ~1.9% + beta ~1.0 x ERP 6.5% = ~8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. Net-cash balance sheet so WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in all scenarios (risk charged once, in the scenario flows and weights); no premium added for the persistent H-share discount, which is a market-pricing fact rather than a cash-flow risk.

Lease liabilities (RMB3.03bn at Dec-25) EXCLUDED from total_debt; total_debt 7,290 = short-term borrowings 545 + current long-term borrowings 236 + long-term borrowings 2,509 + bonds 4,000 at 30 Jun 2026.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100%-consolidated; NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at book (RMB2,913m at 30 Jun 2026; ~10x the ~RMB260-290m/yr NCI profit share). Calibration: modelled FY0 operating NOPAT ~1.6bn + recurring JV share ~1.5bn - after-tax net interest ~0.1bn - NCI ~0.26bn ~= RMB2.7-2.8bn, against FY2025 core attributable profit RMB1,678m that was struck AFTER RMB1,055m of goodwill/asset/credit impairments (KLG Europe goodwill RMB561m); add-back of the non-cash goodwill write-down puts core near RMB2.5-2.7bn, and H1-2026 core profit ran +17% YoY.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with non-US/cyclical adaptations, plus an equity bridge for equity-accounted JVs. Routing: Sinotrans is an operating logistics company (freight forwarding 59%, contract/project logistics 30%, e-commerce logistics 11% of revenue) -- balance sheet is receivables/payables, fixed assets and warehouses, with no deposit funding, no fair-value property model and no investment-company structure, so the bank/REIT/LIC rows do not apply. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). Analysis.json was available and read. OPERATING BASE (FY2025, RMB m): revenue 96,809; operating costs+taxes&surcharges+selling+admin+R&D 96,005 -> 804; plus recurring government logistics subsidies ~1,490 (other income 1,819 less 328 classified non-recurring) -> core EBIT incl ROU depreciation 2,294; plus D&A 2,702 -> EBITDA pre-lease 4,996 = 5.16% (FY2024 same build 4.79%). Excluded from the flows and handled in the bridge: share of JV/associate results (FY2025 recurring RMB1,539m, of which DHL-Sinotrans in the e-commerce segment RMB1,162m; H1-2026 RMB814m), the RMB2.18bn Loscam/REIT disposal gains, fair-value gains, and interest income (RMB158m stripped: net cash 5.5bn > 1x FCF base). Reported FCF 1,433 = OCF 3,086 - capex 1,653; OCF was depressed by a RMB1.4bn working-capital outflow and EXCLUDES the RMB2.55bn of investment income received in cash (investing). Owner FCF last_fcf 1,275 = 1,433 - 0 SBC - 158 interest income. Component year-1 owner FCF (base) ~1.6bn, ~1.7% of revenue, ties to the FY2025 rebuild (EBITDA 4,996 - lease 1,014 - tax 27% on 2,211 - capex 1,653 = ~1,730). SBC-ZERO MARKET: house and street bases coincide; band_position null. Buybacks: RMB479m in FY2025 (A-share plan, completed and cancelled); RMB69m FY2024. NET CASH at 30 Jun 2026 (seasonal low: AR rose RMB3.0bn in H1 as the sea-freight index surged and Sinotrans advanced freight for customers; the 30 Jun cash of 12,791 compares with 17,010 at 31 Dec 2025 -- that working capital should partly unwind, an unmodelled upside of roughly RMB0.2-0.4/share). Cash includes RMB5.8bn (Dec-25) of deposits with China Merchants group finance companies, treated as cash. WORKING CAPITAL: net trade working capital is close to zero (AR+prepayments+other receivables ~ AP+contract liabilities+other payables+wages) and swings with freight rates; wc_capture -2% of revenue change. CASH TAX 27% on operating EBIT: statutory 25% with non-deductible overseas/loss-making subsidiaries; FY2025 segment taxes ~875 on ~2.4bn taxable segment profit.
inputs.jv_treatment: Equity-accounted JVs/associates (book RMB7,487m at 30 Jun 2026) valued at 10x recurring share of profit of ~RMB1,500m (FY2025 1,539 recurring; H1-2026 814 annualises higher; FY2024 1,879 included Loscam, 25% sold in 2025). DHL-Sinotrans pays out essentially all its profit (RMB1,380m dividend received FY2025), so this is a cash stream; 10x is ~ capitalisation at the 8.5% cost of equity with ~-1.5% growth, a deliberate haircut for US de-minimis removal and cross-border express pressure. Matching-asset rule: JV income is excluded from the flows and the JV asset enters the bridge once.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.3% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 2.7% and from core EPS (FY2025 recurring EPS RMB0.23 vs RMB0.48 FY2022). Book growth is retained earnings swelled by non-recurring disposal gains (RMB2.3bn FY2025), not operating compounding; revenue is the steadier anchor for a freight-rate pass-through business.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC ~0 - interest income): FY2020 1,995; FY2022 3,380; FY2025 1,275 (RMB m). The steep FCF CAGRs reflect freight-cycle working-capital swings (FY2022 release, FY2025 build) and that reported OCF excludes JV dividends received (~RMB1.4-2.5bn/yr in investing); they are not a structural decline. SBC is immaterial so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs coincide. Revenue FY2018 77.3bn -> FY2021 peak 124.3bn (freight-rate spike) -> FY2025 96.8bn.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue -3% (H1 -8% on lower rates, H2 lifted by the sea-freight surge since Feb-2026), then 2-3% volume-led growth. Pre-lease EBITDA margin 5.2% in FY2026 on H1 core profit +17%, easing to 5.0% as logistics subsidies (~1.5% of revenue) drift lower and are offset by contract-logistics mix.

bull.narrative: Freight rates hold up through 2026, overseas and contract logistics compound, margin climbs 0.6pp.

bear.narrative: Container oversupply and tariffs compress forwarding; roughly half of the logistics subsidy is withdrawn by year 5; margin falls 1.2pp.

scenario_narratives.base: Freight rates normalise from the early-2026 spike while volumes grow with China's export base. Revenue dips 3% in FY2026, then grows 2-3%. Forwarding stays a thin-spread agency business. Air and rail gains (H1-2026 air +88%, rail off a small base) and Southeast Asia/Middle East expansion roughly offset a slow fade in local-government logistics subsidies (RMB1.62bn FY2025 vs 1.90bn FY2024). Pre-lease EBITDA margin holds near 5.0%, which gives owner FCF of about RMB1.6-1.9bn a year. DHL-Sinotrans keeps paying about RMB1.4-1.5bn a year to Sinotrans. The payout ratio stays around 65%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'new carrier' transformation works: controllable capacity, industry-specific contract logistics (auto/new energy, electronics, chemicals) and overseas networks push direct-customer share and mix up. The China-Europe/China-Asia rail express becomes a structural hedge against ocean volatility. Trade lanes re-route rather than shrink under US tariffs. The REIT platform recycles warehouse capital at a premium to book. Revenue grows 4-5% mid-cycle and margin steps up to 5.8%, still well below global peers like DSV and K+N.
scenario_narratives.bear: Container shipping overcapacity drags spot rates through 2027. The end of US de minimis and further tariff rounds keep shrinking US-lane air freight and cross-border e-commerce, which already drove FY2025's 47% fall in core profit. Forwarding commoditises further as domestic competitors undercut. Policy withdraws about half of the RMB1.6bn logistics subsidy, a third of operating EBIT. More goodwill impairments at European acquisitions (KLG Europe) signal that past M&A destroyed value. Revenue falls 6% then 2%, and margin slides to 4.0%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: earnings are tied to freight rates and US tariff policy, and about a third of operating EBIT is discretionary government subsidy. Base 50%: a net-cash SOE balance sheet and a 65% payout ratio make a solvency-type downside implausible, so the bear case is margin erosion rather than distress. Bull cut to 25%: it needs freight demand, subsidy persistence and mix improvement to all go right at once, and the FY2021-25 record shows rate gains reversing.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sinotrans is valued as three pieces: (1) the consolidated forwarding/logistics operation on an owner-FCF basis, with leases charged as operating cost and subsidies kept in only at their recurring level, (2) the equity-accounted JVs, mainly 50% of DHL-Sinotrans, capitalised at 10x their recurring profit share, and (3) net financial cash and fair-value investments, less minorities at book. The operating business is worth less than the JVs plus net cash. The H-share's ~75% discount to the A-share is why the HKD price sits well below the value of the parts.
key_risks_to_valuation: JV value (~RMB2.1/share) depends on DHL-Sinotrans international express volumes; US de minimis removal and trade conflict could cut its profit
Government logistics subsidies (~RMB1.5bn recurring, ~1.5% of revenue) are discretionary and already falling
Freight-rate cyclicality drives large working-capital swings; the 30-Jun-2026 net cash is a seasonal low
Further goodwill impairment on overseas acquisitions; SOE capital allocation may prioritise policy objectives
The A/H premium has persisted for years; H-share holders may never be paid for the value gap
